name: Install source and installer package
plain: Apps can see which store installed them.
meaning: Shows sideloaded, beta or store installs. Used for fraud and update messaging.

limits.headline: Can see which store installed it, like Google Play or a side loaded file
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app starts up
can: Tell if it came from Google Play or another source on Android 11 or newer
Check this to decide what to show you
Learn a rough clue about the install source on iPhone
cannot: See which store installed other apps
Know on iPhone with the same detail as Android
Be sure the answer is true if the phone is tampered with
limits.differs: Android 11 and newer names the installer. iPhone gives only a rough clue.

story.what_it_is: Apps can see which store, or what other source, installed them.
story.for_you: You never see it. An app knows if you got it from the official store, a beta, or a file. It may nag you to update from the store or refuse to run on a hacked copy.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to spot sideloaded or repackaged apps and to decide which update message to show. It is useful for fraud and for cracked game copies.

use_cases.example: A paid game spots a cracked copy installed from a file and blocks it.
A bank app limits features if it was not installed from the official store.
A security tool flags apps installed from unknown sources.
A team sees how many testers came from a beta channel.
An ad network discards installs from unknown sources as fraud.
A streaming app shows a store update link for the right store.
A company checks that a work app came from its managed store.

story.android_note: Android shows which package installed the app, from API 30.
story.ios_note: Only partial. iOS exposes much less.
